svg.text: The fastest way round a corner is not the obvious one

The same 90° corner, driven twice. Identical car, identical entry speed, identical tires. The only thing that changes is how much straight road comes after it — and the fast line through the corner changes with it.
centreline
direction of travel
apex
apex
30 m of straight after the corner
apex 49% through the corner
slowest 24.6 m/s (89 km/h)
exit 27.5 m/s (99 km/h)
260 m of straight after the corner
apex 55% through the corner
slowest 24.3 m/s (87 km/h)
exit 46.5 m/s (167 km/h)
Nobody told the optimiser what a
racing line is. It was given the tires,
the width of the road, and a stopwatch.
With a long straight ahead, the apex
moves 6 percentage points later —
sacrificing corner speed to get the car
pointed straight sooner, so it can start
accelerating earlier.
Cropped to the corner: 35 m to 163 m along the track. Corner radius 40 m, road 8 m wide, entry speed 32 m/s in both cases. Scale 85 px per 10 m.

[MEASURED] bicycle model + optimal control + Sedan_Pac02Tire.tir · offsets removed · m 1360 kg · 54% front · 200 nodes, 0.82 m apart · [SOURCED] RV-1 parameters §1 · corner geometry [ASSUMED] — a made-up corner chosen to be readable
Minimum-time solve, distance-domain collocation. Slip angles are constrained to ±12° so the answer stays inside the region where the tire model was fitted.
